title: Seamless region failover with data sovereignty guardrails
creator: Luca Romano
description: Summary: Implement policy enforcement and orchestration for multi-zone and multi-region Dedicated fleets to enable automatic failover while preserving data residency constraints and per-customer throughput guarantees. Motivation: customers with regulated workloads require automated failover to maintain availability during zone/region incidents but cannot violate residency controls. We need a predictable, auditable orchestration layer that can: 1) honor per-tenant residency policies, 2) respect reserved throughput commitments (Dedicated capacity SLAs), and 3) perform graceful failover with bounded RTO/RPO. Scope: control-plane policy checks, fleet placement constraints, emergency routing actions, autoscaler integration to preserve throughput targets, observability and audit trails, and a staged rollout (canary -> region pairs -> global). Not in scope: full multi-cloud support (later), major changes to runtime kernel selection logic.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine prevents placement of tenant workloads in regions outside their allowed residency list unless an operator-approved emergency override is recorded

Failover workflow routes traffic to pre-approved warm-standby capacity in same-region or allowed fallback regions and preserves per-tenant reserved throughput at >=95% of target within 5 minutes under typical failure scenarios
Autoscaler respects 'reserved_throughput' field and prioritizes pre-warmed nodes when scaling up during failover
All failover decisions are logged with tenant_id, decision_reason, timestamp, and operator (if any) in the audit trail
Console shows a timeline for failover events, affected tenants, and estimated RTO/RPO; dashboards expose p50/p95/p99 latency and token throughput per tenant during failovers
implementation_notes: Control plane: extend placement service with residency-check hook that returns allowed_regions list for tenant_id; failover coordinator consults same hook before routing
Capacity model: add 'reserved_throughput' and 'preferred_zone_affinity' attributes to Dedicated reservations; mark warm-standby pools and attach cost/latency metadata
Autoscaler: when failover starts set scale_priority=high for tenants with active reservations; use predictive spin-up based on KV cache warming heuristics to reduce first-token latency
Routing: implement staged traffic shift (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with per-step health checks and automatic rollback on error rate spike >5% over baseline
Data residency enforcement: operators can define allowed fallback regions per tenant; any emergency override requires a signed justification recorded in audit_log and triggers a security review entry
Backward compatibility: default behavior for tenants without residency restrictions remains unchanged; older reservations map 'reserved_throughput' to existing quota mechanisms
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated: start with internal test tenants and Redwood staging environment
Canary: enable for 5 low-risk customers in a single regional pair (us-west1 <-> us-central1) for 2 weeks
Expand to region pairs with at least two availability zones and healthy warm pools; monitor QPS, latency, and cost delta for 4 weeks
GA: enable self-serve residency rules in Console and API with audit logs; require ops review for override actions
Post-GA: collect customer feedback and iterate on warm-standby sizing heuristics and cost controls
